subject: Data fencing & operational evidence — Dedicated vs Private VPC
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medicore.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Data fencing questions after our call

Thanks again for the call this morning, Connor. Quick recap from our Security & Infra team: MediCore needs explicit confirmation on three things to evaluate Dedicated vs Private VPC: 1) where customer data (input prompts + generated tokens) is persisted and for how long, 2) which components touch unencrypted data (control plane vs data plane), and 3) proof points for KMS/CMK integration and audit log retention (we need log retention >= 1 year for token tracing).

We're leaning toward a Private VPC because of our regulatory auditors, but we want to make sure Dedicated can be scoped to the same guarantees without a multi-month on-prem procurement. Could you provide a short evidence pack (matrix or one-pager) that maps: data residency, encryption at rest/in-transit, where logs land, and whether control plane metadata may flow through Redwood-managed services? Also include any constraints around BYOK/HSM and whether the control plane can be placed in our VPC boundaries.

I attached our security requirements spreadsheet for convenience (see attachment stub). If it's easier, we can do a 30-min technical sync this week. Appreciate a quick prioritized response — our renewal/expansion approval is timing-sensitive.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Security & Privacy Lead
MediCore Health
Attachments: MediCore_Security_Reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: connor.obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the spreadsheet. High-level reply and proposed next steps below. I've looped in Ben (Dedicated product) and Marissa (security/compliance) to directly address the evidence and operational details.

Quick answers (summary):
- Persistence: By default, Hosted API retains request/response logs per our retention policy (configurable); Dedicated keeps customer inference data on isolated GPU pools, and we can configure aggressive TTLs. Private VPC keeps both control and data planes inside the customer's VPC (no traffic through Redwood-managed subnets).
- Components touching plaintext: Data plane (inference servers) handles unencrypted tokens; control plane metadata (model selection, routing) can be configured to minimize sensitive fields. We can sign an addendum that enumerates fields that are never persisted.
- KMS/BYOK & audit logs: We support external KMS keys (BYOK) for model artifacts and can integrate with customer KMS for certain secrets. Audit logs for Dedicated can be forwarded to your logging endpoints; retention policies are configurable but we will provide evidence for 12+ months.

Requested deliverables and timeline:
1) Security matrix mapping (we will provide a one-page PDF + matrix) — Ben, Marissa: can you confirm we can deliver the matrix and an extracted control-plane/data-plane diagram by EOD Wed?
2) Follow-up 30-min tech sync to go through the matrix and specific clauses — propose Wed 11/18 10:00am ET or Thu 11/19 2:00pm ET.
3) If private VPC is required, we will share the architecture handoff checklist and the expected delivery window (typically 4-8 weeks depending on networking approvals).

Elena — if you prioritize the items in your spreadsheet, we will align the evidence pack to those asks.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien

Hi Elena — following up on Connor's summary with concrete deliverables for Dedicated and where it differs from Private VPC. Attaching our security matrix stub for Dedicated.

Key points for Dedicated capacity:
- Isolation model: Dedicated provisions a customer-dedicated GPU pool and isolated tenant namespace. Data plane (inference) runs on those GPUs and is logically/physically isolated at the tenant level.
- Persistence and TTLs: We can set request/response TTLs to zero (no persistence) or short retention windows; however, short-lived debug logs may be kept for troubleshooting for a configurable period.
- Control plane: For Dedicated, the control plane remains Redwood-managed (model versioning, routing, autoscaling). We can redact sensitive fields before they are sent to the control plane; persistent metadata does not include raw prompt text by default.
- BYOK / KMS: We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/CMEK) for stored artifacts and can enable envelope encryption for certain secrets. HSM-level BYOK (FIPS/HSM) can be discussed with our security PM — highlight if MediCore requires hardware-backed keys.
- Audit logging: We can stream audit logs (request ids, timestamps, model ids, token counts, but not raw tokens) to your logging endpoints (Syslog/CloudWatch/EL) with 12–24 month retention options. If you need raw token tracing for forensic use, Private VPC or on-prem is the recommended path.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-security-matrix.pdf (matrix stub)

Deliverable commitment: Ben/Marissa will share the redwood-dedicated-security-matrix.pdf plus a one-page control-plane/data-plane diagram by 2026-11-18 EOD. If private VPC is required, we'll follow up with the Private onboarding checklist and estimated calendar.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that's helpful. A couple clarifications from our auditors after reviewing your matrix stub:
1) When you say "redact sensitive fields," we need examples of fields that are redacted and an explanation of the redaction pipeline (e.g., where it happens, reversible or irreversible).
2) Audit logging: we need the ability to correlate a raw input to a request id for debugging/regulatory investigation. If Dedicated cannot provide raw tokens in logs under any circumstance, we need to understand the remediation path if an incident requires token-level tracing.
3) BYOK/HSM: MediCore requires hardware-backed keys for production keys in scope of PHI. Please flag if Dedicated cannot meet the HSM requirement; if so, Private VPC with customer-controlled HSM is the path.

We will prioritize items in our spreadsheet and send back the first tab by EOD so you can map deliverables. Also — yes to a 30-min tech sync. Wed 11/18 10:00am ET works for our team. Please send an invite.

Elena
